items.title: Merely-Designated Existence: Six Kinds of Language That Point Beyond Themselves

items.zh: 何等名為假相有法？謂若於是處，略有六種言論生起，當知此處名假相有。何等名為六種言論？謂屬主相應言論、遠離此彼言論、眾共施設言論、眾法聚集言論、不遍一切言論、非常言論。
items.en: What is called a thing existing by a merely designated mark? Wherever, briefly, six kinds of expression arise, know that this is called merely-designated existence: expression dependent on a possessor; expression neither directly naming this nor that; expression by common convention; expression by aggregation of many things; expression not applying universally; and expression naming what is impermanent.

items.zh: 屬主相應言論者，謂諸言論，配屬於主方解其相，非不屬主。如說生時、此誰之生，待所屬主起此言論。謂色之生，受、想、行、識之生。非說色時，此誰之色，待所屬主起此言論。如生如是，老、住、無常等心不相應行，隨其所應盡當知。是名屬主相應言論。
items.en: Expression dependent on a possessor: whatever expression can only be understood once it is attached to some governing thing, and not otherwise. As when one says "arising" — arising of what? — the expression only makes sense once attached to its possessor: the arising of form, or of feeling, perception, formations, or consciousness. This is called expression dependent on a possessor.

items.zh: 若於是處起此言論，當知此處是假相有。

遠離此彼言論者，謂諸言論，非以此顯此，亦非以彼顯彼，是說名為遠離此彼言論。若以此顯此言論，是言論亦於實相處轉，亦於假相處轉。若以彼顯彼言論，是言論亦於實相處轉，亦於假相處轉。若非以此顯此，亦非以彼顯彼言論，是言論一向於假相處轉。云何以此顯此言論，於實相處轉？如言地之堅。云何此復於假相處轉？如言石之圓。如地之堅、石之圓，如是水之濕、油之滴、火之煖、燬之焰、風之動、飄之鼓、亦爾。云何以彼顯彼言論，於實相處轉？如言眼之識、身之觸，如是等。云何此復於假相處轉？如言佛授德友之所飲食、車乘、衣服、莊嚴具等。云何非以此顯此，亦非以彼顯彼言論，一向於假相處轉？如言宅之門、舍之壁、瓶之口、甕之腹、軍之車、林之樹、百之十、十之三、如是等。
items.en: Expression neither directly naming this nor that: expression that neither fully names one single thing by itself, nor names two genuinely separate things joined together. As when one says the door of a house, the wall of a dwelling, the mouth of a jar, the belly of a jug, the chariot of an army, a tree of a forest, ten within a hundred, three within ten, and so on.

items.zh: 眾共施設言論者，謂於六種相狀言說自性，假立言論。六種相狀者，一、事相狀，二、所識相狀，三、淨妙等相狀，四、饒益等相狀，五、言說相狀，六、邪行等相狀。事相狀者，謂識所取。所識相狀者，謂作意所取，能起於識。淨妙等相狀者，謂觸所取。饒益等相狀者，謂受所取。言說相狀者，謂想所取。邪行等相狀者，謂思所取。眾法聚集言論者，謂於眾多和合，建立自性言論。如於內色、受、想、行、識，建立種種我等言論；於外色、香、味、觸等事和合差別，建立宅、舍、瓶、衣、車、乘、軍、林、樹等
items.en: Expression by common convention: expression provisionally established in common by beings, on the basis of six observable features. Expression by aggregation of many things: expression provisionally established by taking a self-nature from the coming-together of many things — as with "house," "dwelling," "jar," "robe," "chariot," "army," "grove," or "tree."

items.zh: 不遍一切言論者，謂諸言論，有處隨轉，有處旋還。如於舍宅舍宅言論，於諸舍宅處處隨轉；於村、聚落、亭邏、國等、即便旋還。於盆甕等盆等言論，於盆甕等處處隨轉；於瓶器等，即便旋還。於軍軍言，隨諸軍轉；於別男女幼少等類，即便旋還。於林林言，隨諸林轉；於別樹根、莖、枝、條、葉、華、果等類，即便旋還。非常言論者，由四種相應知。一、由破壞故；二、由不破壞故；三、由加行故；四、由轉變故。破壞故者，謂瓶等破已，瓶等言捨，瓦等言生。不破壞故者：謂種種物共和合已，或丸或散，種種雜物差別言捨，丸散言生。加行故者，謂於金段等起諸加行，造環釧等異莊嚴具，金段等言捨，環釧等言生。轉變故者，謂飲食等於轉變時，飲食等言捨，便穢等言生。如是等類，應知名為非常言論。隨於諸物發起如是六種言論，當知此物皆是假有。是名
items.en: Expression not applying universally: expression that applies without obstruction to one thing, but fails and withdraws when applied elsewhere. Expression naming what is impermanent: expression arising through destruction, through non-destruction yet rearrangement, through deliberate working, or through transformation — as when a shattered pot no longer bears the name "pot," or transformed food no longer bears the name "food."

blocks.text: Today's reading is a short treatise on language. Some things "exist" only as designations: the meaning of a word that points beyond the word to something else. The treatise names six kinds. Several short passages are untranslated (0362a11, 0362a28, 0362b10, 0362b28), and the Ru-Yi English paraphrases a few lines (logged in the correction list); the commentary follows the Chinese.
**Merely designated existence** (假相有) is what we refer to through six kinds of expression:

items: **Possessor-dependent** (屬主相應): words like "arising", "ageing", "impermanence" need a possessor: whose arising? Master Cháng Bǎi: all twenty-four formations dissociated from mind are of this kind (Day 21). The *Pīxún jì*: such notions are "guests", having no substance; the things they depend on are the "hosts".
**Neither this nor that** (遠離此彼): "the door of a house". Venerable Miào Jìng: "the house is not the door, yet apart from the house there is no door."
**Dependent on another** (觀待於彼): long and short, father and son, named only in relation.
**Aggregation** (眾法聚集): many things gathered and called by one name: an army, a forest, a self. Master Cháng Bǎi: talk of "self" falls here: the aggregates gathered and named.
**Not universal** (不遍一切): words that apply in some places and not others. Venerable Miào Jìng: "house" applies to all kinds of houses but not to villages.
**Impermanent** (非常言論): names that stop applying when things change. Master Cháng Bǎi: gold ingots worked into bracelets are no longer called ingots.

blocks.text: Venerable Miào Jìng: "When this person is born he has no name; we assign him one, Buddha-given, or Virtue-friend." Names are imposed. One person finds someone beautiful, another does not, Master Cháng Bǎi adds; both are personal designations.

Venerable Miào Jìng sums up: all six "are transformations from various conditions coming together; then human knowledge names them." Master Cháng Bǎi draws a practical benefit: once one understands this, "one is no longer turned by others' tongues and suffers less." Praise and blame are designations too (Day 116).

This is the linguistic side of the imagined nature: much of what seems solid in experience is language, laid over a flow of conditions. Seeing that is not denying the world; it is seeing which parts of it are words.

quiz.q: Possessor-dependent expressions like "arising" need a possessor. What range does Master Cháng Bǎi assign them?
options: all twenty-four non-associated formations are possessor-dependent expressions — merely designated
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "So all twenty-four non-associated formations are possessor-dependent expressions, all merely designated." Venerable Miào Jìng cites birth, ageing, duration, and impermanence as distinctions on the aggregates.

quiz.q: How does the Pixunji use "guest" and "host" to explain possessor-dependence?
options: guest is the Buddha, host beings
the imagined, having no substance, is the guest; the underlying thing with its own substance is the host
quiz.why: The *Pixunji*: "Because such imagined notions have no substance, they are called guests; the things they depend on, each having its own substance, are called hosts." Arising and ageing attach to the aggregates.

quiz.q: "The door of a house" exemplifies "neither this nor that." How does Venerable Miào Jìng describe house and door?
options: the house isn't the door, yet apart from the house there's no door — general and particular, neither one nor different
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "The house is not the door, yet apart from the house there is no door — they differ as whole and part, neither one nor different." f16 omits the passages on the other two types.

quiz.q: Among the omitted passages, "naming that by that" has the designated example of "Buddha-given" and "Virtue-friend." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain it?
options: a person is born nameless and given names like Buddha-given or Virtue-friend — names are imposed designations
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "When this person is born he has no name; we assign him a name, Buddha-given, or Virtue-friend." Master Cháng Bǎi: "eye's consciousness" is real; "Buddha-given's food" is designated.

quiz.q: Impermanent expressions include those arising "through deliberate working." What example does Master Cháng Bǎi give?
options: gold ingots smelted and worked into bracelets — they are no longer called ingots
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: impermanent expressions through working refer to gold ingots smelted and fashioned into bracelets and ornaments. The four cases: destruction, rearrangement, working, transformation.

quiz.q: What practical benefit does Master Cháng Bǎi see in mastering the six designated expressions?
options: one is no longer turned by others' tongues and suffers less — knowing that oneself and others speak much of designated things
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: having mastered these principles, one is no longer turned by others' tongues and suffers less, knowing that oneself and others speak of many designated things.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng sum up the things named by the six expressions?
options: all are changes from the coming together of conditions, then named by human knowledge — all designated
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "They're all transformations from various conditions coming together; then human knowledge sets up all kinds of names — these are all designated." f16 omits the section's concluding sentence.
